questions.prompt: A handler on tool_call throws an error while checking a call. What happens to the call?
options: The tool runs anyway, because the handler did not block
The tool does not run, and the model gets an error result
pi retries the handler until it succeeds
pi skips the handler and checks the schema again
questions.explanation: A handler that throws also stops the call. The error becomes an error result, so the gate fails closed.

questions.prompt: A handler changes event.input.sql to a new string. What does pi do next?
options: It checks the new value against the schema again
It ignores the change and uses the model's original value
It runs the tool with the new value and does not check the schema again
It asks the model to confirm the new value
questions.explanation: pi performs no re-validation after mutation, so a handler that changes an argument must keep it valid.

questions.prompt: Why does the SQL pack open shop.db read-only when the gate already blocks non-SELECT statements?
options: A second independent layer still protects the data if a query slips past the pattern
Read-only files make the gate run faster
pi requires every database to be read-only
questions.explanation: The gate and the read-only database are independent. If a query passes the pattern, the database still refuses to write.
